# Acute promyelocytic leukemia

Acute promyelocytic leukemia is defined by the t(15;17) translocation that creates the PML-RARA fusion gene.
All-trans retinoic acid is given at 45 mg/m2 per day during induction.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a common presenting complication of this subtype.
Auer rods are needle-shaped cytoplasmic inclusions formed from fused azurophilic granules.
Faggot cells contain bundles of Auer rods and are typical of the hypergranular form.
Arsenic trioxide induces degradation of the fusion protein and is used with retinoic acid.
Differentiation syndrome presents with fever, weight gain, pulmonary infiltrates and serous effusions after treatment starts.
Dexamethasone is the treatment of differentiation syndrome while therapy is continued where possible.

# Other subtypes

Core binding factor leukemias carry t(8;21) or inv(16) and have a favourable prognosis with high-dose cytarabine consolidation.
Mutations in FLT3 with internal tandem duplication predict relapse and are targeted by midostaurin during induction.
The standard intensive induction for fit adults combines cytarabine for seven days with an anthracycline for three days.
